Great — below is a complete, practical family road‑trip plan (Seattle → San Antonio → Austin → Houston) for your April 10–18 Spring Break trip. I prioritized kid-friendly choices, kept a realistic budget under $3,000, and flagged where you can save money.

If you want, I can tailor hotels to exact nightly rates from your desired booking site or check real-time rental prices — just give me permission to look up current rates.

1) Rental car
- Recommended category: Compact SUV / midsize SUV (examples: Toyota RAV4, Hyundai Tucson, Ford Escape).
  - Why: Comfortable for 2 adults + 2 kids + luggage, better visibility and cargo than a compact car, more comfortable for 3+ hour drives. A minivan is ideal for space but usually adds substantial cost.
- Estimated cost (7–8 days, one-way SAT → HOU/HOU):
  - Low estimate (compact SUV, advance booking, discount): ~$450–$600 total (includes taxes and one-way drop fee).
  - Mid estimate (mid-size SUV): ~$600–$800 total.
  - Notes: one-way drop fees between Texas airports often run $150–$300; rates spike if booked late.
- Pickup/drop-off:
  - Pickup: San Antonio International Airport (SAT) on April 10 (afternoon).
  - Drop-off: Houston Hobby (HOU) is the best match for your return flight HOU→SEA; it’s closer and often cheaper than IAH (Bush). Be sure to request a HOU drop when booking.
- Tips for best deals:
  - Book now — one-way fees and availability change quickly during spring break.
  - Compare aggregator sites (Kayak, Expedia) and then check the rental company site — sometimes direct rates are better.
  - Use any memberships (Costco Travel, AAA, AARP) — these can cut daily rate or waive some fees.
  - Choose “pay at pickup” only if you want refund flexibility; otherwise prepaid often cheaper.
  - Check for included mileage and confirm unlimited miles for inter-city travel.
  - Inspect the vehicle carefully (photos of any damage) and consider the collision-damage waiver only if your auto insurance or credit card does not cover rentals.

2) Hotels (family-friendly picks)

San Antonio (3 nights: Apr 10–13) — near Riverwalk
- Budget / Best value: Drury Plaza Hotel San Antonio Riverwalk
  - Approx price: $150–$210/night
  - Pros: Free hot breakfast, evening snacks/drinks, indoor/outdoor pool, suites available, excellent Riverwalk location
  - Cons: Can be busy; older rooms than luxury properties
  - Why good for kids: free snacks + pool and central walking access to kid attractions

- Mid-range: Hyatt Regency San Antonio Riverwalk
  - Approx price: $200–$270/night
  - Pros: Prime Riverwalk location, comfortable rooms, family rooms available, on-site dining
  - Cons: Higher cost, can be crowded
  - Why good for kids: immediate access to Riverwalk, easy walking to The Alamo and riverboat

- Budget alternative: Holiday Inn Express San Antonio-Riverwalk Area
  - Approx price: $130–$180/night
  - Pros: Lower price, free breakfast, newer rooms
  - Cons: Short walk to Riverwalk (not right on it)
  - Why good for kids: lower price frees budget for activities

Austin (4 nights: Apr 13–17) — walkable to South Congress or downtown
- Budget / family-friendly: Hyatt Place Austin/Downtown or Hyatt House Austin/Downtown
  - Approx price: $150–$220/night
  - Pros: Suites (with sofa bed), free breakfast (Hyatt House), good downtown location, family rooms
  - Cons: Less boutique vibe than SoCo hotels
  - Why good for kids: extra space, convenient to Lady Bird Lake and downtown family attractions

- Mid-range / South Congress access: Hotel San José or South Congress Hotel (if available within budget)
  - Approx price: $220–$350/night (SoCo hotels can be pricier)
  - Pros: Walkable to South Congress shops, great dining nearby, local Austin vibe
  - Cons: More expensive; some are boutique (smaller rooms)
  - Why good for kids: easy walk to shops, music, and evening activities (and bat viewing nearby)

- Budget alternative further south: La Quinta or Holiday Inn Express near SoCo
  - Approx price: $120–$170/night
  - Pros: Lower cost, often free breakfast
  - Cons: Slightly less walkable depending on exact location
  - Why good for kids: helps stay under budget while still close to attractions

Note on pricing: April is shoulder/peak season with festivals and warm weather; book now for the best rates. Choose hotels that include breakfast and/or a kitchenette for big savings on food.

3) Day-by-day itinerary (family of 4, kids 8 & 11)

San Antonio (April 10–13)
- April 10 — Arrival (afternoon)
  - Pickup rental at SAT, drive to Riverwalk hotel (30–40 min incl traffic).
  - Light activity: check in, quick Riverwalk stroll, Riverwalk dinner (family-friendly Tex-Mex/BBQ). Consider a short narrated riverboat cruise (30–35 min) — relaxing after travel and a fun intro to the city.
  - Early bedtime; hotel pool if kids need to burn energy.

- April 11 — Full day (classic San Antonio)
  - Morning: Visit The Alamo (free; short visit) then stroll Alamo Plaza.
  - Late morning/lunch: Market Square (El Mercado) for tacos and local snacks.
  - Afternoon: San Antonio Zoo or DoSeum (children’s museum) — both are excellent for your kids’ ages. If hot, the zoo is partly shaded; DoSeum is interactive and great for hands-on play.
  - Evening: Hemisfair Park (playground) and Tower of the Americas (for views). Early family dinner on Riverwalk.

- April 12 — Full day (adventure & nature)
  - Option A (nearby adventure): Natural Bridge Caverns (guided tour, above-ground attractions); good for curious kids who like caves/rocks.
  - Option B (city & history): Witte Museum (kid-friendly science/history exhibits) + San Antonio Missions National Historical Park (walk or short bike ride along Mission Reach).
  - Evening: Riverwalk lights + optional short night river cruise.

- April 13 — Morning before checkout
  - Quick option: Brackenridge Park miniature train (if running) or Japanese Tea Garden (short walk and koi ponds), or a short visit to the DoSeum if you missed it.
  - Midday: Check out, drive to Austin (I-35 N, ~1.5–2 hrs). Suggested stop en route (see Driving Routes).

Austin (April 13–17)
- April 13 — Arrival (afternoon/evening)
  - Check in to hotel near South Congress or downtown.
  - Walk South Congress (music shops, tacos, fun shops), dinner on SoCo.
  - If time and energy: watch bats at Congress Avenue Bridge at sunset (bats are usually active in April; early evening emergence is dramatic).

- April 14 — Full day (outdoor & iconic Austin)
  - Morning: Zilker Park exploration — Zilker Botanical Garden if interested; Zilker Zephyr miniature train can be a hit.
  - Lunch: picnic or family-friendly food trucks.
  - Afternoon: Barton Springs Pool (if weather is warm — kids love the spring-fed pool) or paddleboard/kayak on Lady Bird Lake (rentals available).
  - Evening: casual dinner downtown or on SoCo.

- April 15 — Full day (interactive & museums)
  - Morning: Thinkery (Austin’s children’s museum) — hands-on exhibits perfect for 8–11 year-olds.
  - Afternoon: Explore the Texas State Capitol (free tours) and nearby grounds; then try a local barbecue spot or live music lunch (many family-friendly spots mid-day).
  - Evening: Explore South Congress shops; maybe live music with earlier family shows.

- April 16 — Full day (day trip or more Austin experiences)
  - Option A: Hamilton Pool Preserve day trip (reservations needed — check early). Beautiful nature, but watch for swim restrictions.
  - Option B: Inner Space Cavern in Georgetown (cavern tours) + downtown Georgetown square (less driving)
  - Option C: Visit the Austin Nature & Science Center + Mayfield Park & Preserve (peacocks!) for a relaxed day.
  - Evening: last night on SoCo or a family movie/pizza night.

- April 17 — Morning: check out, drive Austin → Houston (HOU)
  - Depart early to avoid afternoon traffic (I-10 E, ~2.5–3 hours).
  - Stop at Buc-ee’s (fun pit stop for kids & snacks) and/or Bastrop State Park for a stretch.
  - Drop rental at HOU mid/late afternoon. Check into a hotel near Hobby Airport for early morning flight prep.

April 18 — Return flight HOU → SEA (morning)
  - Short airport commute to accommodate check-in/security.

4) Top 5 kid-friendly must-do activities (ages 8–11)

San Antonio:
1. River Walk boat tour — short, fun, gives an easy orientation to the city.
2. The Alamo & nearby Alamo Plaza — historical basic tour (short attention span friendly).
3. DoSeum (San Antonio children’s museum) — hands-on STEM and play exhibits.
4. Natural Bridge Caverns (or San Antonio Zoo) — caves or animals depending on interest.
5. Japanese Tea Garden + Hemisfair playground — easy, pretty spot for photos and play.

Austin:
1. Thinkery (children’s museum) — great for interactive learning/play.
2. Zilker Park & Barton Springs Pool — big open space and swimming if weather permits.
3. Congress Avenue Bridge bat viewing (at sunset) — very popular and memorable for kids.
4. Lady Bird Lake kid kayak/paddleboard (guided or rental) or the Zilker Zephyr train.
5. Texas State Capitol tour + nearby playgrounds and food trucks.

5) Driving routes & stops

- SAT → Austin
  - Route: I‑35 N from San Antonio to Austin.
  - Approx drive time: 1.5–2 hours depending on traffic (about 80–85 miles).
  - Recommended stops: 
    - New Braunfels / Gruene (historic district; tubing and shops in season; Gruene Hall a fun photo spot).
    - Lockhart — famous BBQ (short detour off I‑35) — lunch stop if the family likes BBQ.
    - Buc‑ee’s near Luling: clean bathrooms and kid-crazy snacks.
  - Tip: depart early to avoid I-35 commuter traffic into Austin.

- Austin → Houston (HOU)
  - Route: I‑10 E (most direct to Houston Hobby area) or TX‑71 E / I‑10 depending on exact destination.
  - Approx drive time: 2.5–3 hours (about 165–175 miles).
  - Recommended stops:
    - Bastrop for a quick stretch and state-park views.
    - La Grange (Chimney Rock/Monument Hill) or Buc‑ee’s for snacks.
    - Brenham/Chappell Hill (if you want Blue Bell Ice Cream — small detour north of Hwy 290).
  - Fuel stops: Buc‑ee’s, major gas stations along I‑10 (use GasBuddy to find cheapest stops).

6) Budget breakdown (recommended cost-conscious plan to stay under $3,000)
Estimated totals for your family of 4 for April 10–18. I provide a “budget plan” (to hit under $3,000) and a “mid-range” estimate so you can choose.

Budget plan (recommended to meet $3,000)
- Rental car (7–8 days, compact SUV, one-way SAT → HOU): $550
- San Antonio hotels (3 nights) — budget hotel with free breakfast: $450 ($150/night)
- Austin hotels (4 nights) — budget hotel or suite-style: $640 ($160/night)
- Activities (entrance fees, riverboat, Thinkery, caverns, etc.): $250
- Food/dining (moderate — mix of dining out + hotel breakfast + picnic): $560 ($70/day)
- Gas (approx 500–700 miles): $100
- Misc / contingency (parking, tolls, extra snacks): $150
- Total: $2,700

Mid-range plan (more comfort)
- Rental car (mid-size SUV): $700
- San Antonio hotels (mid-range Riverwalk): $600
- Austin hotels (mid-range/SoCo): $880
- Activities: $350
- Food/dining: $700
- Gas: $120
- Misc/contingency: $150
- Total: $3,500 (over budget)

Key places to trim costs to keep under $3,000:
- Choose hotels that include breakfast or a kitchenette.
- Book a compact SUV rather than mid-size; use Costco/AAA rates.
- Limit paid activities to top picks (e.g., riverboat + 1 museum + cave or zoo) and mix with free activities (parks, bridge bats).
- Eat casual — food trucks, picnic lunches, early dinners; avoid expensive sit-downs every night.

7) Practical tips & packing checklist

Apps and planning tools:
- Navigation & traffic: Google Maps, Waze.
- Road trip planning & stops: Roadtrippers (route stops), GasBuddy (cheapest gas), Yelp/OpenTable for restaurants.
- Activities & reservations: Tripadvisor/Viator for tours, the specific attraction websites to reserve timed entry (Thinkery, Natural Bridge Caverns, Hamilton Pool).
- Entertainment: Audible, Spotify playlists, family podcasts (e.g., “Wow in the World”), offline games app and downloaded movies for kids.

What to pack in the car (essentials for kids 8 & 11):
- Refillable water bottles + small cooler for snacks.
- Wet wipes, hand sanitizer, motion sickness meds if needed.
- First aid kit and basic meds.
- Chargers, phone mount, headphone splitters or two pairs of headphones.
- Lightweight blanket and travel pillows for naps.
- Change of clothes and swimwear/towels in case of spontaneous pool or Barton Springs visit.
- Trash bags and ziplock bags (for wet clothes or trash).
- Small backpack per kid with activity kit (coloring, cards, magnetic games).

April-specific events / notes
- San Antonio Fiesta: Fiesta San Antonio is often held mid-April and can affect hotel prices and crowding. Check the exact 2026 Fiesta dates — if your travel overlaps, book early and expect busier Riverwalk and some road closures.
- Austin bats: April is a good month to see the Congress Avenue Bridge bats emerge at sunset — an exciting free evening activity for kids.
- Wildflowers: Central Texas wildflowers (bluebonnets) often peak in March–April — good photo opportunities on quieter county roads (but never walk into private fields).
- Hamilton Pool: requires reservations and sometimes has swim restrictions; check and book early.
- Weather: early–mid April in Texas is usually pleasant (daytime 65–80°F; evenings cooler). Pack layers and light rain jacket in case of showers.

Quick prioritization checklist to do now
1. Book the rental car (one-way SAT→HOU) and lock in the one-way drop — rates climb fast.
2. Reserve hotels with free breakfast to save money.
3. Book any timed-entry attractions (Thinkery, Natural Bridge Caverns, Hamilton Pool) if you plan to visit.
4. Download entertainment and playlists/podcasts for kids before travel.
